order.why: Zoom shows 21002 is a spurious break inside a perfectly straight 65cm track (170 deg prong pair, the rule-1 trap), and the track Braggs cleanly at 21000, so it must start at 21001, whose single 190k terminal point reads as a vertex blob.

Low-energy knot at z~2: 13003 is the deg-2 apex where a 6.7cm proton leaves and stops at 13000 with a 248k Bragg while a MIP prong leaves the other way at 102 degrees, the 170k reading on both prongs at 13003 being shared vertex charge.

Deg-3 hadronic star with three short heavy prongs, the most upstream real structure in a compact downstream-corner event; alternative is 17002 with its 18 cm proton Bragg (267k) 24 cm further downstream.

Whole 381 cm cluster is one straight MIP line (principal frame a2,a3 ~ 0), so the mid-track knot of short segments is the only vertex-like structure; I pick 6009 for its 85k proton stub and lower z, but 6005 20 cm away is nearly as good.

Rule 1 textbook: deg-4 junction at the lowest z of the cluster with 3 of 4 prongs rising away (mu x1.34, pi+ x1.83, e-shower x1.59) plus a 2.4 cm 480k proton stub; the 67 cm muon's far end 14007 carries a Michel, confirming that end is downstream.

Heuristic 7: p4 shows the 24.6 cm electron trunk runs flat at MIP for its first 13 cm out of 11003 and then jumps to 90000-140000 for the last 10 cm, i.e. a single track that starts here and then showers, so 11003 is the apex; it is also the only degree-2 junction and carries a pi+ stub, but a 28-cluster blob keeps it off certain.

p4 shows seg 26004 rising along the stopping-muon template over the last 5 cm into 26008, so by rule 3 that is the far end and 26006 is the origin - the only candidate in this badly fragmented event with any rises-away.
Rule 1: dQ/dx rises monotonically 42k->211k along the whole 66cm cluster, so 14001 is its unique cool start end.

Only multi-prong junction in the event: a 9 cm proton rises 90k->250k monotonically away from 22002 to a Bragg at 22001, and the other two prongs are MIP-cool at their far ends with their hot patch confined to the dense junction core; the whole cluster hugs the x=-200 anode so the reading is not clean.

Ignoring the 317cm crossing track, the compact complex at (-45,-105,420) gives 40034 as its deg-3 junction with all three prongs non-decreasing away and a hot 6.8cm 110k stub attached, but 17002 and 40031 are nearly as good and the pieces are separated by centimetre-scale gaps.

Only structure in the event is a single 19.5 cm stopping proton whose profile falls monotonically along the brown template from 260k at 5000 to ~90k at 5002, so 5002 is the start end (and it is also the lower-z end).

Rule 1 is 2 of 2 rising away with genuine monotone Bragg rises at both far ends (275k at 18001, 165k at 18002), but the two prongs leave 18003 at 177 degrees so the trap-3 collinearity caveat drops this a tier.
Near rule 8 - the only real object is a 5.8cm hot stub whose p4 profile rises away from the 4000 end; all else is sub-cm unmeasured blips.

Rules 6/7 on a fragmented two-arm EM event with no track; picked the degree-3 apex of the largest shower cluster where a short 2.2-MIP stub attaches, but both arms look like photon conversions so the true vertex may be invisible.

Rule 1: the event is a single 62 cm track whose p4 profile is a textbook monotone stopping-muon Bragg rising to 310k at 10006, so the cool end 10000 is the only vertex candidate with its segment rising away.

Rule 1: p4 shows seg 9004 rising monotonically over its last 5 cm to 150k at 9001 (continuing into the 4.6 cm 175k stub to 9003), a genuine Bragg, so 9001/9003 is the stopping end and 9000 is the cool end everything points away from; every rival candidate is a 0-prong sub-cm blob with no dQ/dx opinion.

No degree-3 junction anywhere and all dQ/dx flat; clusters 46 and 11 lie almost collinear in the principal frame, so I took the deg-2 end 46037 (which carries a 2.3 cm stub) nearest the gap between them - close to a guess.
Rule 1 at 20002: the 146 cm muon leaves MIP and Braggs at 20000 while the 40 cm proton chain 20006+20005 rises 80k->260k away from 20002, and 20002 is the lowest-z junction.

Rule 1 on the p4 profile: the 5 cm proton falls monotonically 320k->180k from 16010 to 16011, so it stops at 16010 and starts at 16011, which sits inside the loose cloud of soft fragments; the 466 cm cluster-11 track is straight (175 deg at 11004) wall-to-wall MIP with no Bragg at either end.

The 224 cm cluster-23 track is flat MIP end to end while skimming the y- floor from the z=500 corner, i.e. a through-going cosmic with no Bragg and no real Michel, leaving the 14.1 cm proton as the interaction; its charge rises monotonically 125k to 305k toward 34005, so the vertex is its cool origin 34004.

Cluster 10 is an entering-top-face stopping cosmic, leaving only cluster 18, where 18011 is a localized 120-140k core with both prongs cooling away from it and prong B re-rising to 82k at 18015; 18014 6.6 cm upstream is the rule-1-clean rival.

Rule 3 decides it: the 111 cm track follows the stopping-muon template up to 200k over its last 10 cm at 4001 with two blobs beside that end reading as a Michel, so 4001 is the far end and 4000 is the start; no other candidate in the event has any rule-1/6/7 support.

Rule 7 locates the junction confidently - a 35 cm track meets the shower apex across a 51 deg kink - but 17000 and 60026 straddle it 1.9 cm apart and only the shower back-extrapolation (1.3 cm to 17000 vs 1.9 cm the other way) breaks the tie, so the id is close to a coin flip.

Rule 1 plus the hot-patch test: p4 shows a broad Bragg-shaped 120-130k plateau decaying away from the 9002 end, while the 9001 end is a single isolated 110000 point on an 80k baseline, i.e. vertex charge rather than a stopping rise.

Rule 1 2-of-2 at a 97 deg kink: the 39 cm proton climbs monotonically along the proton template to 172k at 7001, and the 191 cm muon's other end 7000 carries a 2.5 cm MIP-level Michel stub after its own Bragg, so both prongs point away from 7003.

Only interior deposit in an event of three disconnected fragments is the 219k proton stub, with a companion blip just past 24005 implying travel outward from 24004, but the stub is flat at both ends so there is no real directional evidence.
The 358cm track Bragg-spikes to 145k in its last 2cm with a decay stub, so it is a stopping muon; only an isolated 1cm 90k blip is left to pick.

Rule 6/7 on a compact 65cm shower: 4003 is the only real junction (deg 4, prongs of 21.9 and 15.5cm plus a 3/4.6cm stub), sits at the upstream low-x corner, and the whole spray including the six satellite blips opens away from it. Rule 1 fails there but three particles cannot all stop at one point, so I read it as a dense EM start.

Single 81cm track: dQ/dx is continuous across the break 12002 (76k vs 81k) and the 5cm stub is flat 80k with no Bragg of its own, so 12002 is a spurious break and the cool free end 12001 is the track start; the only Bragg is at 12000.

The whole cluster is a single 31 cm stopping proton - p4 rises monotonically from 95000 to 200000 at 8000 - so 8001 is its cool start end and therefore the interaction point; nothing else in the event is larger than a blip.

Rule 3 removes 13001, where the 246 cm track has a monotone Bragg rise to 150k with a blue 25-40k Michel on that same end, and rule 1 then leaves 13000 as the only cool end the track gets hotter away from; the tier is low because the track runs backward in z from 13000 and no prong corroborates it.
Rule 1: 126.6 cm muon rises away x2.60 to a Bragg at 10000 while a 2.6 cm 158k proton stub sits on the vertex, with more hot proton fragments within 10 cm in the zoom.

p4 shows dQ/dx continuous and monotone across 11002 into 11003 (MIP to 145k to 390k), so cluster 11 is one particle Bragging at 11003 and 11002 is a far end not a junction; the remaining structure is a shower opening in +x/+z from the hot 120-168k apex at 59032 (rule 7).

Both long muons cool into the same 4 cm junction region and stop hot at their far ends (10000 at 100k, 10001 at 137k with a 10 cm e-like cluster 70 hanging off it - rule 3 Michel), and 10003 is the degree-4 hub of short p/e/pi stubs that the two long prongs radiate from; the 10002/10004 alternatives sit 2-4 cm away.

Rule 1 gives 3002 (2 of 2 prongs rise away, 55k in the middle) but only 3001 is a genuine monotone template Bragg - the 3000 end is a 2cm hot patch, not a rise - so the two-Bragg reading is weak; unclear for the 174 degree prong pair, with 3000 the live alternative 10cm away.

The chain cluster86 -> 14 -> 89100 -> 89101 -> 88098 rises monotonically to 260k at 88098, so the particle travels +y and stops there; that puts the origin at the bottom of the low-charge cluster-86 tangle, where the p5 cone opens best (+1.4 cm), but the event is diffuse.

Rule 7 plus rule 1: in the principal frame the whole event opens out as a cone from a1=-50 and 18016 is at that narrow apex, with a 7.9 cm pi+ leaving it and stopping hot (108k) at 18001 while two e prongs head downstream into the widening shower.
Rule 1 at a 125 deg junction: a 143 cm muon rising away to 114564 and a 13 cm proton sitting at 173736-191654 throughout, a classic muon-plus-proton vertex.

p4 resolves cluster 19's knot: two heavy prongs both leave 19004 cool at 70-75k and rise away to hot stops at 19003 and 19008, while the 39.6 cm prong's charge simply fades to 2k across the bridge from 19002, so 19004 is the true cool origin despite its 172 degree pair; the rival region is a spray with no apex.

Two-Bragg-ends trap: 11001 (200k) and the 11002/11000 arm (160k) both point away from the 11003 kink, which itself carries a hot blob; rule 2 favours the upstream 11001 but is not allowed to overturn rule 1.
